title: Pre-unification grounding: exhaustive crosslink CLI-surface inventory + Thermite architecture refresh (latest pull) -> knowledge pages -> design-impact audit

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: GROUNDING SET progress: (1) run-record-capability-inventory REGISTERED (the WAS-side oracle page; knowledge-cache bad-ref repaired via remote prune first). (2) thermite-architecture-refresh REGISTERED — basis 84d276e7 (bootable multicore kernel, Stage 4 + Gates G3/G4 since our last capture). Five audit-critical findings: the CONTROL-PLANE META-GATE (their crosslink incident #93 — 'crosslink init' regenerated settings.json and silently de-wired the spec-discipline + anti-pattern hooks for the entire Stage-3 arc; fixed by tooling/control-plane-check.py, a CI gate asserting every required hook's wiring + script exist, with restore snippets — vsdd has the IDENTICAL init-regeneration exposure, cf. #856's deployed-payload fragility; this seeds a vsdd control at hook-wiring grain, the installed-artifact-integrity check's sibling); the canonical REQ registry with POLICY-BEARING statuses (shipped/retired final + evidence-required, partial/blocked/deferred require remaining-scope — the successor to the binary shipped/not-started rule); RECEIPT-BOUND closures (artifact publishes only with a receipt binding sources/contracts/toolchain digests/transcripts, honest scope labels, replay-to-byte-identity, publication-path-absent-on-failure — #840 seed material); PER-CLAUSE trust migration (solver success never moves trust; failed replay stays solver-trusted AND audit-listed — the fully-worked name-the-grade model); estate-page corrections queued for the audit (R-SIDE-1/R-BV-1 shipped not candidates; new R-BAT-1; acto agents pin model fable; rotating-seed daily watchdog; doc-drift on synthetic merge commits). Still in flight: crosslink CLI surface (5 scope extensions), crosslink non-CLI integration surfaces (MCP servers + file protocols + daemon + trust), mdatron capability surface, incident-corpus index, runtime-harness surface. Then the design-impact audit.
